package_info.package_versions: N/A (attack technique, not a package version)
package_info.why_malicious: Magecart is a digital skimming attack that injects unauthorized JavaScript into eCommerce checkout pages to steal customer payment and personal data. The malicious code exfiltrates sensitive information, such as credit card details and personal identifiers, to attacker-controlled domains without user or merchant consent, directly violating privacy and payment security standards.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a customer loads the cart or checkout page and interacts with payment fields
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the JavaScript of the cart or checkout page (client-side), often via compromised third-party scripts or direct injection
required_permissions: DOM access (to read form fields containing payment data)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the customer loads the checkout page and enters payment information, the code reads payment form fields (card number, expiration date, CVV) from the DOM, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in immediate exfiltration of sensitive payment data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code programmatically accesses sensitive payment fields and transmits their values to an external, unauthorized domain, which is a hallmark of digital skimming attacks and is never required for legitimate payment processing.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted, PCI-compliant payment processors, never to unknown or unapproved external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors or analytics scripts may collect form data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints with strict data handling policies.
key_indicators: Direct access to payment form fields (e.g., card number, expiration date, CVV) via DOM selectors
Outbound network requests (POST) to domains not associated with the merchant or known payment processors
Execution specifically on sensitive pages such as cart or checkout

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a customer loads any page containing personal data forms and enters information
execution_context.file_location: Injected into site-wide JavaScript or included via compromised third-party scripts
required_permissions: DOM access (to read form fields and cookies)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a customer loads a page with personal data forms and enters information, the code reads the email field and browser cookies from the DOM, then sends this information via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling exfiltration of personal data and session information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects personal data and session cookies and exfiltrates them to an unauthorized external domain, which can facilitate account takeover, session hijacking, or further targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should never transmit personal data or authentication cookies to unknown third parties; such data should only be sent to trusted, privacy-compliant endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics scripts collect user data, but only to trusted, privacy-compliant endpoints and never include sensitive session cookies.
key_indicators: Access to personal data fields (e.g., email) and document.cookie
Network requests (POST) to non-whitelisted or suspicious domains
Execution on pages containing login, registration, or checkout forms

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the cart, checkout, or site-wide pages via compromised third-party scripts or direct injection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming and data leakage code in customer browsers.

attack_chain.action: The malicious code collects sensitive data (payment information, personal data, cookies) from the DOM as customers fill out forms.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of stolen data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected data is sent via network requests (e.g., HTTPS POST) to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data, enabling fraud or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript accessing payment or personal form fields (e.g., card number, email) on checkout, cart, or login pages
Client-side scripts making network requests (POST) to domains not associated with the merchant, payment processors, or approved analytics providers
Exfiltration of sensitive data immediately after form submission or field entry
file_indicators: Unexpected or unauthorized JavaScript files loaded on checkout, cart, or login pages
Changes in third-party script content or the appearance of new, unrecognized script inclusions on sensitive pages
network_indicators: POST requests to domains such as 'attacker-domain.com' or 'malicious-analytics.com' that are not associated with payment processing or analytics
Outbound traffic from checkout or login pages to unknown or unapproved external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor and scan client-side scripts on cart, checkout, and login pages for unauthorized access to sensitive form fields and outbound network requests to unapproved domains. Implement integrity checks for all third-party scripts and alert on any changes or new inclusions. Block or alert on any script that attempts to exfiltrate data to unknown endpoints. Regularly audit the list of domains present on sensitive pages and ensure only trusted payment and analytics providers are allowed.
